title: centaurea transcaucasica subsp. alexandri
intro: Centaurea transcaucasica subsp. alexandri, commonly known as Alexandrian knapweed or Caucasian cornflower, is a plant species in the sunflower family. It is used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, which help to protect against cell damage and reduce inflammation in the body. The therapeutic actions of Centaurea transcaucasica subsp. alexandri include its ability to act as an antiseptic, antimicrobial, and anti-inflammatory agent, making it useful in treating wounds, infections, and skin conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
